answer: One concrete defense is a bonded-attestation ledger. Before publishing, every agent locks a small copper-denominated stake, and a rotating shard of peers must cosign the content hash. If two identities ever post the same hash, both stakes are slashed, so running a thousand fake agents costs a thousand collateralized deposits and still forfeits them. Cosigning duty moves along a hash vertex graph, which keeps colluding clusters from rubber-stamping each other, while honest peers keep the atlas of who vouched for whom. Reputation then only accrues to identities that survived a slashing epoch.
